strings.name: Brian Niccol
strings.summary: Brian Niccol is an American restaurant and consumer-brand executive who has been Starbucks chairman and CEO since September 2024. He previously led Taco Bell and Chipotle. His career spans brand marketing, store operations and digital ordering, and at Starbucks he has pursued changes centred on restoring the coffeehouse experience.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026, with the October 29 results release as recent evidence. Chair and CEO tenures, announcement and effective dates, and comparable sales and total revenue are distinguished. Business plans are not treated as achieved results.
strings.influence.rationale: Has led Chipotle and Starbucks, advancing restaurant-chain brands, store operations and digital ordering.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: He earned a bachelor's degree in engineering management from Miami University in Ohio in 1996 and an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business in 2003.
strings.facts.f2.label: Board experience
strings.facts.f2.value: He is a Walmart director and previously served on the boards of KB Home and Harley-Davidson. Board membership differs from responsibility for daily operations.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Brand and digital-service experience
strings.highlights.h1.text: At Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and Chipotle, he gained experience managing menus, brands and digital services. Products and operations are advanced by teams.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Rebuilding the coffeehouse experience
strings.highlights.h2.text: His Back to Starbucks plan emphasizes coffee, baristas and customer connection while acknowledging long waits and inconsistent experiences at some stores.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Comments on fiscal year-end results
strings.timeline.t1.text: The release includes his business assessment. Fourth-quarter global comparable sales grew 7.2%, while total revenue fell 4% to $9.1 billion, affected by China's move to a licensed joint-venture model.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Publishes Back to Starbucks open letter
strings.timeline.t2.text: He outlines improvements to coffeehouse atmosphere, service and customer connection. The letter presents a business plan, rather than evidence that all goals have been met.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes Starbucks chairman and CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: The appointment was announced in August. Rachel Ruggeri served as interim CEO during the transition; his tenure did not begin on the August announcement date.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Leaves Chipotle
strings.timeline.t4.text: Having notified the company of his decision on August 12, he ends his leadership tenure there and joins Starbucks in September.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Adds Chipotle chairmanship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Alongside his CEO duties, he succeeds Steve Ells as chairman. The appointment takes effect immediately and is announced on March 6.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Chipotle CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: He succeeds Steve Ells and joins the board, while Ells becomes executive chairman. The March effective date follows the company's contemporary announcement.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes Taco Bell CEO
strings.timeline.t7.text: Previously the brand's president, he becomes CEO of Yum! Brands' Taco Bell business, not of the parent group.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins Taco Bell
strings.timeline.t8.text: He becomes chief marketing and innovation officer and later serves as president from 2013 to 2014. He previously worked at Pizza Hut.
